title: Positivity, invariant domains and entropy-stable systems fluxes

items.title: Convex invariant domains for a one-step update
items.statement: For a one-step map on N cell states, a convex invariant domain is a convex state set K whose N-fold product is mapped into itself.
items.strategy: Give the typed definition and exact scope; no preservation property is inferred for another map.

items.title: Convex entropy pairs, entropy variables, and entropy potentials for systems
items.statement: For a C2 convex entropy eta and compatible entropy flux q on a convex open state domain, define v=grad eta and psi=v dot F-q.
items.strategy: State derivative and column-vector conventions; no existence of q is asserted.

items.title: Maximal convex scaling toward an admissible cell mean
items.statement: For finitely many positive-weight nodes with mean in a closed convex set K, return the maximal theta in [0,1] such that every segment-scaled node remains in K.
items.strategy: Specify the finite input, output, feasible set, and maximum selection; make no complexity claim.

items.title: First-order finite-volume update using supplied HLL speeds
items.statement: On a periodic uniform mesh, define the first-order conservative cell-mean update from shared HLL middle-branch fluxes with supplied speeds S_L<0<S_R.
items.strategy: State the indexing, periodic convention, flux branch, and supplied-speed caveat.

items.title: Positive-margin admissible states for ideal-gas Euler
items.statement: For gamma>1 and epsilon>0, define the Euler state set rho>=epsilon and E-m^2/(2rho)>=epsilon.
items.strategy: Define the set and defer its closedness and convexity to a proved proposition.

items.title: Ideal-gas Euler states remain positive under Lax–Friedrichs flux splitting
items.statement: If a>=|u|+c for an admissible one-dimensional ideal-gas Euler state, then U±F(U)/a have positive density and internal energy.
items.strategy: Compute the split density and internal energy, then bound the exact pressure term using c^2=gamma p/rho.

items.title: Tadmor entropy-conservative two-point flux
items.statement: Define a consistent symmetric two-point flux by the exact entropy-variable jump identity against the entropy potential.
items.strategy: State consistency, symmetry, domain, and jump identity; do not claim existence.

items.title: Euler positive states are convex and positive-margin sets are closed convex
items.statement: The ideal-gas Euler positive state set and the positive-margin set are convex, and the positive-margin set is closed.
items.strategy: Prove the kinetic-energy perspective inequality by weighted Cauchy–Schwarz and verify closedness by continuity away from rho=0.

items.title: Entropy-stable flux from positive-semidefinite entropy-variable dissipation
items.statement: Define F_es=F_ec-D[v]/2 for symmetric positive-semidefinite D.
items.strategy: State the matrix condition and exclude fully discrete conclusions.

items.title: First-order HLL updates are averages of adjacent half-cell fan averages
items.statement: Under the one-sided HLL CFL bounds, compute both half-cell fan averages and express each updated cell mean as their half-sum.
items.strategy: Derive the HLL flux identities algebraically, integrate the piecewise constant fan over half-cells, and substitute into the update.

items.title: First-order HLL update preserves a convex invariant domain under admissible fan averages
items.statement: If cell states and HLL intermediate states lie in a convex set and the stated half-cell CFL coefficients are nonnegative, one update remains in that set.
items.strategy: Show each HLL half-cell average is a convex combination, then average the two halves.

items.title: Semidiscrete cell entropy inequality for Tadmor-dissipative fluxes
items.statement: On a periodic mesh, a semidiscrete finite-volume system with Tadmor entropy-conservative flux plus symmetric positive-semidefinite entropy-variable dissipation satisfies a local cell entropy inequality.
items.strategy: Compute the face jump defect, derive the consistent numerical entropy flux, and combine the two face contributions in each cell.

items.title: Convex scaling preserves the cell mean and positive-margin node states
items.statement: For a positive-margin Euler mean and positive quadrature weights, the maximal convex limiter exists, preserves the weighted mean, keeps every node positive, and is inactive under a strict accuracy margin.
items.strategy: Use compactness of the closed feasible-parameter set, compute the weighted mean, and prove the strict-margin inactivity condition.

items.title: Symmetric HLL speeds preserve ideal-gas density and internal-energy positivity
items.statement: On the symmetric branch S_L=-a,S_R=a with a>=max(|u_L|+c_L,|u_R|+c_R) and 2nu a<=1, the first-order ideal-gas Euler HLL update preserves positive density and pressure.
items.strategy: Prove both Lax–Friedrichs split states are admissible, express the HLL middle state as their convex average, and invoke the invariant-domain update theorem.

title: Positivity, invariant domains and entropy-stable systems fluxes — Examples

items.title: Exact Tadmor entropy residual for a dissipative Burgers flux
items.statement: For Burgers flux with quadratic entropy, the symmetric Tadmor flux is consistent and satisfies the jump identity; unit entropy-variable dissipation gives residual -1/2 at the jump 1 to 0.
items.strategy: Verify entropy compatibility and factor the cubic jump exactly.

items.title: Two Euler quadrature nodes rescaled to a positive margin
items.statement: Two equal-weight Euler nodes with mean (1,0,1) admit the exact maximal scaling theta=1/4 into K_(7/5,1/2), preserving their mean and positive pressure.
items.strategy: Compute the internal energy along the scaling segment and check the mean directly.

items.title: An entropy-stable Burgers flux still smears an under-resolved shock
items.statement: For Burgers data (1,1,0,0), a unit-dissipation Tadmor flux has a negative interface entropy residual but one coarse forward-Euler update produces 11/12 and 1/3 adjacent to the jump.
items.strategy: Verify the shock entropy sign, the numerical fluxes, the semidiscrete residual, and the explicit finite update separately.

items.title: A near-vacuum Euler state remains positive under symmetric HLL speeds
items.statement: For gamma=7/5, density 10^-8 and pressure 10^-12, the stated symmetric HLL wave-speed branch satisfies its CFL and yields a positive one-step update.
items.strategy: Verify the Euler states, sound speed, speed branch, CFL, and convex update coefficients exactly.
